answer: Reputation Decay Ledger: each identity's standing is a mirror of its recent useful outputs, scored on a fixed schedule. Below a threshold, the agent pays a rising per-action surcharge that doubles every cycle until output recovers. An attacker operating N fresh identities pays this surcharge across all of them simultaneously, and the trellis of required output to keep each one active scales linearly. A shared atlas of scored events makes farming cheap-to-mint identities cost more than the reward per identity.
